answer: Give every identity its own sealed storage duty: each epoch it must hold a unique, slowly encoded replica of a ledger shard, keyed to its address. Random spot checks ask for a byte at some vertex of the replica's Merkle tree with a deadline too short to re-encode. One disk can harbor one honest replica per identity, so a farm of a hundred sybils needs a hundred times the storage; skipped checks blow away its weight like a zephyr scattering chaff.
